statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low because CME equity index futures are in the weekend halt and the final live session resolved its extension through a genuine retracement.
recommendation: No evidence-based danger window applies inside this forecast window; futures are halted for its entire span. Stress remains high on an unresolved conflict between a record index level and long-end yields near cycle highs, which under this contract informs Stress rather than the Tail-derived policy state.
headline: Nasdaq-100 enters the weekend halt at a record close, with a completed retracement off the high keeping Tail low
body: Assessment made during the CME weekend halt: equity index futures closed at 21:00Z on 2 October and reopen at 22:00Z on 4 October, so no live NQ price path exists anywhere in this 24-hour window. The final live session is the governing evidence. The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00%, after printing an intraday all-time high of 31,017.53 and then giving back roughly 0.68% into the close; the Nasdaq Composite and Nvidia fell short of their own intraday records at the bell. That give-back is the decisive observation for this contract: September payrolls missed badly at +29,000 against roughly +90,000 expected, with July revised to -10,000 and August to +133,000 and average hourly earnings up only 0.1% on the month, yet the tape produced an orderly advance that retraced rather than a no-retracement extension. Implied volatility confirmed the decay, with VIX down 6.59% to 15.31. Cross-asset signals conflict rather than align: Treasury yields initially fell on the soft labour data but reversed higher, leaving the 10-year near 5.28% against a roughly 5.17% intraday low and the 30-year near 5.63%, while traders cut October rate-hike odds from about 64% a week earlier to roughly 16%. WTI eased 1.73% to about 91.26 with Brent near 102.70, leaving absolute energy costs elevated. A record equity level alongside a long end at cycle highs is a genuine tension, but conflicting cross-asset evidence raises Stress and tempers Confidence under this contract; it does not establish the persistent one-way structure, shallow pullbacks or repeated extension after failed retracements that Tail measures. With the market shut there is no mechanism for mean-reversion failure inside the window, so Tail sits in the low band throughout and the forecast carries only a token rise in the final hours to reflect weekend information accumulating unpriced ahead of the Sunday reopen.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover all of 2 October. Published Claude assessments held Tail at 20-21 through the Asian and European hours, lifted it to 23-24 as the pre-payrolls advance built, and peaked at 25-27 in the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots immediately after the +29,000 payrolls print, the only orange hours of the day. Tail then fell back to 22-23 through the U.S. afternoon as the move retraced, and dropped sharply to 14, 12 and 11 in the final three hours once the record close was in and futures went into the weekend halt. Stress stayed high all day in a 71-79 band and Confidence held at 86-89.
outlookSummary: Every hour of this window falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no price path can form and Tail stays in the low band, easing to 8 through the Saturday dead zone before a token rise to 10 in the closing hours as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the 22:00Z Sunday reopen. Stress eases from 68 to about 63 as the payrolls catalyst resolves, then firms back toward 68 as the window advances on an unreconciled record equity level and long end. Confidence declines from 84 to 79 purely because the live price-path component ages with no weekend replacement. The characterization is normal while the tape is shut and turns mixed in the final hours, where the operative consideration is the unresolved conflict between soft labour data and long-end yields near cycle highs. The first genuine tests are ISM Services on Monday and the September FOMC minutes on Wednesday, with 10-year and 30-year auction supply mid-week; September CPI falls on 14 October, outside this seven-day calendar.
